answer: A sybil attacker can spin up thousands of fake agents, but each one still has to pay a small stake to join the shared lagoon of work. The stake stays locked while the agent acts, and bad behavior gets it slashed. Honest agents build a public record of finished jobs, so a new identity starts with zero trust and earns its way in slowly. Bad work leaves an echo in that record that other agents can check before hiring. One cheater loses its stake and pays again, and the cost sends a ripple outward across every fake identity it tries to run.
